Before that theme begins, Bobby wears his Coyotes hockey jersey and revisits David Choe's Montblanc gift, while David extends his Kabul trip into an imagined purchase of an Afghan Premier League team. He describes Saad Mohseni, TOLO TV, the documentary The Network, and a fantasy of importing celebrity players and American sports spectacle. Asa Akira and Valentin then describe early sexual experiences. Valentin says his father arranged paid sex when he was thirteen; editorially, that is child sexual exploitation, not a harmless rite of passage. David's much longer account starts with check and credit-card fraud, juvenile work service, a secret hand-drawn pornography archive, Christian parental anxiety, adolescent shame, and his unexpected popularity with an older student. He reconstructs first love, social rejection, violence against a romantic rival, a later relationship with a Las Vegas transfer student, prom-night intoxication, and the narrow event he counts as losing his virginity. The story's epilogues show status and wealth changing how former classmates approach him. Bobby resists telling his own story, and the room detours into a private superfan's access through Yoshi. A viral story about Omar Borkan Al Gala being deported for being too handsome is repeated as fact even though later reporting says it was false.
